newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: British Gas unit to award fuel supply pact.
newsitem.headline: British Gas unit to award fuel supply pact.

text.p: First Gas Holdings Corp, the joint venture between First Philippine Holdings Corp and British Gas Plc, said on Tuesday it will soon award a 15-year fuel supply contract for its 990-megawatt power plant in Batangas, in the northern island of Luzon.
A FGHC official told Reuters the winning bidder will supply 30,000 to 35,000 barrels of condensate daily.
"We will name the preferred supplier possibly within the week. We have narrowed down our choices from about eight companies to three big foreign firms," said the FGHC official.
The official, however, declined to disclose details.
"Under this fuel pact, we can terminate the contract once we decide to switch to natural gas," the official added.
FGHC is choosing between liquefied natural gas (LNG) and natural gas from the Camago-Malampaya in the southcentral Palawan island as the final fuel to run its 990-mw power plant.
The power plant is expected to be operational by 1998.

"If we choose Camago gas we have to wait until the gas is harnessed in 2001 and if we pick LNG, it will take three years to put the storage facility in place. Either way, we can't wait so we need an interim fuel pact," the official explained.

The official said condensate was chosen as the temporary fuel to run the 990-mw power plant due to its low sulphur content and competitive price. Aside from condensate, FGHC earlier mulled the use of naphtha and distillate.
